item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
在美国职场遇到的几个 Toxic Manager，本科背景都很普通，是巧合还是认知差距？

看到地里一个帖子，讲入职 TikTok 三个月就开始崩溃，包括无休止的加班、Aggressive 的企业文化，以及部分管理层的低素质行为。

我在美国职场遇到的三个 Toxic Manager，都是国内本科院校相对普通的管理者，认知水平让人难以接受。

这让我想到自己过去十多年的职场经历。

本人在美国做了十多年 Data Science / Machine Learning，现在主要做 AI Engineering，经历过金融、科技等不同领域的公司。

回头看，自己遇到的几个最 Toxic 的老板，居然也有一个共同点：国内本科背景都比较普通，而且在专业认知、技术判断和管理方式上存在明显问题。

尤其是最近 AI 发展这么快，有些管理者对 LLM、Agentic AI、AI Coding Tools 的理解相当有限，却非常喜欢干预技术实现细节。

明明有成熟工具和框架可以利用，偏偏要求工程师从头手搓。既没有合理的技术论证，也不考虑 Engineering Efficiency、Opportunity Cost 和实际 Business Value。

更让人难以接受的是，他们往往不愿意听取技术专家的意见，反而非常自信，喜欢 Micromanagement，用职位权力代替技术讨论。

当然，我并不认为普通本科毕业的人就一定认知水平低，也认识不少非名校出身但技术优秀、管理能力很强的人。

但这些经历确实让我开始思考：

第一学历和一个人长期的认知水平、学习能力、思维方式，甚至管理风格，到底有没有相关性？

高考毕竟在一定程度上筛选了学习能力、逻辑思维和自律程度。虽然工作十几年后，学校的重要性已经大幅下降，但早期形成的思维习惯、对知识的态度以及自我认知能力，会不会长期影响一个人的职业发展？

另外还有一种可能：真正的问题不是学历，而是某些管理者本身缺乏专业能力，又特别需要通过控制下属来维持权威。

想听听地里大家的真实经历：

1. 你们遇到的 Toxic Manager，有没有什么共同背景或特征？
2. 大家觉得第一学历和一个人的认知水平、管理能力有多大关系？
3. 在 AI 发展这么快的今天，遇到技术认知落后、却坚持指导每一个实现细节的老板，大家一般怎么处理？

纯粹分享个人观察，样本量有限，不想搞学历歧视。也很好奇大家有没有相反的经历，比如普通本科出身但非常优秀的 Manager，或者名校毕业却非常 Toxic 的老板。

item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
Meta vs TikTok，求选 offer 建议

楼主最近在考虑两个 offer，想听听大家的建议。比较看重未来的成长和发展。

Meta：之前实习过，拿到了 return offer。对团队和工作环境比较熟悉，也挺喜欢的。TC 300k 左右，HR 说不能 compete。

TikTok：TC 430k 左右。薪资更有吸引力，而且还没 compete 过，不过对这边的工作强度和长期发展了解得没有那么多。

现在主要纠结的是，Meta 的团队和环境比较熟悉，也确实挺想去，但是薪资差距不小。TikTok 给得更多，但不太确定工作强度和未来发展怎么样。

想问问大家，如果是你们会怎么选？尤其想听听大家对个人成长、WLB 和以后跳槽机会的看法。

看地里大家对🦑和tt 的评价都不怎么好，所以也不知道怎么选了😂

item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
挂一位西雅图绝经哥

标题为挂人，但想想还是只讲事实，先给人一次机会

某西雅图大厂Z哥是我来美国以来见过的最恶心猥琐的中国人了，很不幸跟您老在一组，算是前世作孽今生来渡劫。

此公在小组午饭之后猥猥琐琐来打听我dating和情感状况，得知楼主找得到对象以后又打听楼主对象年龄，我也是想尽早摆脱此人，随口说“对象年龄比我大一点”，此公竟然说：

“那 她 绝 经 了 怎 么 办？”

？

？？

？？？

EXM？？？？

您老要不要自己听听自己在讲什么？楼主当场感到生理不适立马扭头就走了，已正式考虑提交HR ticket希望找HR好好跟此老聊一聊。不要说你不懂职场言行举止行为规范，也不要狡辩你是出于关心/开玩笑/文化差异才讲这种抽象话。绝经哥你自己咋不找老板或者组内女同事问问“你/你对象绝经了怎么办”？你要想立nerd人设就请做戏做全套，不要只对同级讲冒犯的话OK？看人下菜碟，天天触碰他人底线也要有个限度，OK？

楼主也是中国留学生过来的，深知独自在美国打拼的不易，平时对国人的抽象行为都是睁一只眼闭一只眼，能帮就帮一下，谁知道善人招苍蝇，这次实在是越想越觉得恶心加猥琐。我犹豫了一下没把你真实姓名、工作具体地点、公司、毕业学校挂小红书和一亩三分地是想再给你一次机会，下次不只是“西雅图大厂”、“Z哥”这么简单了，绝经哥你要是刷一亩三分地刷到这个帖子意识到是在说你就老老实实来找我道个歉。

另外请教一下，这种情况应该怎么收集证据递交HR部门？要不要每次和绝经哥交流都开个录音？

item.title: Avi Chawla Chat with video using EmbeddingGemma 2 (100% local): EmbeddingGemma 2
item.description:
Avi Chawla
Chat with video using EmbeddingGemma 2 (100% local):

EmbeddingGemma 2 by @GoogleDeepMind maps text, images, video, and audio into a shared vector space. This makes it possible to search video frames with natural language.

Devs have already built native Rust implementations for local inference.

Unsloth also provides a 176 MB, 4-bit GGUF checkpoint for text embeddings, although that version doesn't include the full multimodal pipeline.

I tested the video-search use case by building a chat interface that finds matching frames and jumps to their timestamps.

On my Apple M3 Pro, using the CPU:
- Indexing took 29s for a 60s video
- Search took 25 ms on average across 9 queries
- The saved frame vectors occupied 180 KiB.

The video is indexed once. Each new search embeds the query and compares it with the saved frame vectors. Processing stays entirely on the laptop.

The video below depicts the entire flow in action.

That said, model quantization reduces the memory needed for the weights. The retrieval index has its own storage cost, which grows as you add videos.

To dive deeper into reducing that cost, I wrote a full article on binary quantization.

It explains how storing vectors with one bit per dimension reduces their raw storage by 32x compared with float32, and includes a working retrieval implementation.

Read it below.

https://t.co/UVK8C699vj - Avi Chawla

item.title: Crypto-常山赵子龙 #BTC #ETH 不得不说老徐是真的懂技术的，对UID的这个分析逻辑技术人员一看就能明白，但非技术人员可能理解起来有点费劲； 其实C
item.description:
Crypto-常山赵子龙
#BTC #ETH
不得不说老徐是真的懂技术的，对UID的这个分析逻辑技术人员一看就能明白，但非技术人员可能理解起来有点费劲；

其实CZ也是技术出身，应该是确实好久没有一线参与币安的管理了，所以币安会存在这种从技术和产品上看上去都有点不太合理的逻辑；

我来简单说一下。

这首先是一个非常基础的技术设计和账户安全问题。

在 OKX 品牌下，我们坚持一个基本原则：

不同站点之间，UID 要么在全局范围内保持唯一，要么就不允许用户仅凭 UID 进行跨站点内部转账。

原因很简单：UID 是账户标识。如果同一个品牌不同站点可能存在相同 UID，却又允许通过 UID 跨站点转账，就可能造成收款账户识别错误和资金误转风险。

千里之堤，溃于蚁穴。所有重大风险都是由很多个小缺陷积累而成。

很难理解，为什么这么简单的一个问题，会演变成简中 X Crypto 社区的一个热点。

更令人不解的是，居然还有那么多账号针对一位由于某平台缺陷导致资产损失的用户进行谩骂、人身攻击，同时替相关平台洗地。

究竟是什么样的企业文化和价值观，在背后推波助澜？ - Star_OKX
tweet

item.title: Naval RT @Briankeating : I am a professor at the @UofCalifornia . I am appalled
item.description:
Naval
RT @Briankeating: I am a professor at the @UofCalifornia. I am appalled by the conduct of one of its Regents, Scott Galloway, appointed in August by Governor Newsom.

@profgalloway is one of only 26 voting Regents entrusted with governing a university system serving hundreds of thousands of students & employing tens of thousands of faculty & staff.

Twice, first on a live Pivot episode featuring Hillary Clinton & on Prof G with Fareed Zakaria, Galloway called Elon Musk a “traitor to the West.”

He invoked Julius & Ethel Rosenberg, who were executed for espionage, and declared that Musk should be held to the same standards.

He didn’t explicitly demand Musk’s execution. But invoking the deaths of two convicted spies while calling an American citizen a traitor makes the implication hard to miss.

Musk has not been convicted of treason. Indeed, “treason against the West” isn’t even an actual crime.

Now imagine UCLA alumnus @BenShapiro, appointed a UC Regent, saying the same about George Soros.

Would the Governor defend his right to serve? Would Regent leadership shrug and call it provocative commentary? Or would there be demands for resignation?

But there’s something worse here than another of Scott’s trademark podcast rants.

He sits on the Regents’ Academic & Student Affairs Committee.

The committee’s charter says it oversees student conduct, faculty conduct, academic personnel, & campus climate, among other responsibilities.

This is not some honorary title.

The Board sets university policy, controls institutional budgets, & appoints senior university leadership.

You can unsubscribe from a podcast.

A student who finds Scott’s comments morally repugnant can’t unsub from the Regents.

UC bylaws require Regents to serve the public trust with a “high degree of ethics and candor,” including as private citizens.

Professors owe students intellectual integrity. Regents bear an even greater duty: they govern institutions that teach it.

Yet a Regent serving on the committee responsible for student & faculty conduct invokes executions while labeling a fellow citizen a traitor.

What does that say to our students?

That intellectual restraint is expected of the governed but optional for those who govern?

That standards of conduct depend on whether the target of your rhetoric is politically fashionable to despise, as long as the audience applauds?

This isn’t about defending @ElonMusk. He needs no defense from me.

Nor is it about silencing Scott. As if that were possible. He’s free to express his opinions, however reckless they may be.

But freedom of speech is not freedom from accountability, and holding a university office of public trust is not an entitlement.

There is an enormous moral chasm between exercising your right to speak recklessly and demonstrating the judgment required of one of the 26 people who govern our great public university.

The UC Board of Regents isnt a podcast sponsors can boycott. It’s a public trust.

One final irony. At @NYUStern, Galloway teaches Brand Strategy, including a session on crisis management.

His own prescription for leadership in a crisis is unequivocal: acknowledge the problem, have leadership take responsibility, and “overcorrect.”

He’s praised the departure of corporate leaders as evidence of effective crisis management.

Now Galloway himself sits on the UC Board of Regents.

Will he hold himself to the standards he teaches, or does accountability apply only to other people’s institutions?

Professor lecture thyself!

I believe Scott Galloway should seriously consider whether his continued service on the Board of Regents is consistent with the ethical standards and responsibilit[...]
